cards.text: King David's not done organizing yet. He and the commanders of the army set apart some of the sons of three men: Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun.

cards.question: David and the army commanders set apart some sons of Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun. What are those sons set apart to do?

answers.text: Guard the gates of the city

cards.text: Army commanders picking the band, I LOVE it. First up, Asaph's sons: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah and Asarelah, all under the direction of their father.

cards.question: Asaph's sons work under Asaph. True or false: Asaph himself prophesies under the direction of the king.

cards.text: Next come Jeduthun's six sons, from Gedaliah to Mattithiah, under their father, who prophesies with the harp. Six sons plus a dad on the harp, I bet the neighbors NEVER got a quiet night.

cards.question: Jeduthun prophesies with the harp. What is he doing as he plays?

answers.text: Giving thanks and praise to the LORD
Warning the king about his enemies
Mourning over the sins of the city

cards.text: Then come the sons of Heman, the king's seer: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel and on down to Mahazioth. Every one of them was given to Heman through the promises of God.

cards.question: Heman's sons were given to him through the promises of God. What for?

cards.text: God had given Heman fourteen sons and three daughters. Seventeen children, Heman? I looked after six little cookie cutters in the Millers' kitchen and thought I was busy.

cards.question: The sons play cymbals, harps and lyres under the direction of their fathers. What is all that music for?

answers.text: The service of the house of God
The king's court at the palace

cards.text: Counting their relatives, they number 288. Then they cast lots for their duties, kind of like drawing names for the office gift swap, just with a LOT more on the line.

cards.question: Those relatives are all trained and skillful in the ___ of the LORD.
True or false: When the musicians cast lots for their duties, the teachers got to sit it out.

cards.text: Then the lots fall, twenty-four in all, starting with Joseph from Asaph's family. Every lot is a man, his sons and his brothers, 12 in all, and twenty-four groups of 12 is your 288, right on the dot!
